utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Court Deputy, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-95-12-PT, The Prosecutor versus Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I have the appearances, please. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, my name is Josee D'Aoust. With me today is Mr. Roeland Bos, and our case manager, Mrs. Lakshmie Walpita.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. D'Aoust.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Where is Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, Your Honour. Mr. Scott could not be here today. He is out of the country. He apologises for his absence and asked me to attend in his place. But he is out of the country and could not attend the Status Conference today, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You mean, you have been entrusted by Mr. Scott to appear.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Zeljko Olujic, attorney-at-law from Zagreb, Croatia. I'm counsel for Mr. Ivica Rajic. Colleague Doris Kosta is on the Defence team with me. However, she is not present today. So I'm appearing on behalf of my client alone today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Rajic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have any problems in following the proceedings, please do not be hesitant to let me know. You may sit down, please. Following the filing of the amended indictment on the 14th January, a second initial appearance of the accused was held on the 29th January 2004. The Trial Chamber is required pursuant to Rule 65 bis to hold a Status Conference within 120 days of the initial appearance of the accused to organise the exchange between the parties to ensure expeditious preparation for the trial and to allow the accused to raise any issues in relation to the status of his case, including his mental and physical conditions. Mr. Rajic, would you please stand up. Do you have anything to complain at this stage concerning your conditions in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about your health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. The Defence filed a second motion challenging the form of indictment on 23rd of February 2004 following the submission of the amended indictment by the Prosecution on the 14th of January 2004. The Prosecution responded on the 5th of March 2004, and the Trial Chamber issued its decision on the 27th of April 2004. In that decision, we request the Prosecution within 30 days of the date of this decision to clarify the apparent inconsistencies on a number of the victims as presented in the paragraphs 16 and 17. Now I turn to the Prosecution. I want to know how much time and in what form do you need to file something concerning the amendment in this aspect?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We -- the clarification can be done very shortly. We don't need much delay to do that. And we can file an amendment to those paragraphs indicating the reason, or we can file an explanation with the Trial Chamber and counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Do you think you need another amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: I think that the clarification can be -- maybe expressed without the amending indictment because the facts are there. It may, as the Court requests us to need to clarify, but I don't think it needs an amended indictment. Maybe clarification can be filed with the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next issue is about disclosure. Pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), the Prosecution shall provide the accused with copies of the supporting material and all prior statements obtained by the Prosecution from the accused within 30 days of the initial appearance of the accused. The supporting materials submitted in support of the amended indictment was provided to the Defence on the 15th of January 2004, except for the B/C/S translation for four English documents which were provided on 29th January following the initial appearance. As far as the Chamber knows, the Rule 66(A)(i) has therefore been complied with. The Defence requested further information on the source of a series of documents obtained by the Prosecution from the archives of the secret service of the Republic of Croatia in order to be able to check their authenticity. I believe that the Defence referred to about 10 to 20 million pages. The Defence was supposed to draw the least of those documents for which it sought further information. I would like to know whether the parties have already solved this issue or not. And this time, I'll give the floor to the Defence first.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It is true, as you have stated, that on the 15th of January 2004 we received additional material. We have been working on it. We have studied it. It is also true that the Defence raised an objection at the last Status Conference where we stated that it would be fair on the part of the OTP and in order to reach the truth if they could at least roughly give us an indication how they gained access to certain material at the Croatian State archives. It is true, as you have stated, Your Honour, that on that occasion I said that that involved 10 million pages put in different boxes. In the meantime, the archives service has started selectioning that material, and we have already managed to carry out some authentication, however, not in its entirety. I will ask from my learned friend Mr. Scott in accordance with your instructions to be given information as to sources so that I can verify the authenticity of the material. What I can say is that I have managed to track down about 70 per cent of the material because the archives has classified some of the material, so the Defence was able to verify the authenticity. However, for a small portion of material, we will need the additional information. And in accordance with your instructions, I will request this additional information from the Prosecution within the following month. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could I turn to the Prosecution on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Regarding the request, Your Honour, as it was mentioned at the last initial appearance, it's difficult for us to provide specific information if we don't necessarily know which documents are causing a problem. But if Defence counsel wants to be a little bit precise and tell us which document in question he would like to have information, if it's in -- if we're able, we will provide the information to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm surprised to hear that there's so many documents involved in this case. I think as a principle, we should reduce the paperwork as much as possible at this stage. And the -- I believe that all those documents first of all should be related to this very case, and there should be some probative value. Thirdly, those documents could possibly be used during the trial proceedings. If we spend a lot of energy on seeking those documents and at last we do not use it, what's the purpose to go into that amount of the documents? Although the Defence counsel said that they have already finished about 70 per cent of those documents, the left documents will still amount to thousands of pages. I hope the parties could meet together to have this problem solved. And it is my belief that Defence counsel is waiting to submit a list for those documents they want to know the source. But Defence counsel have to remember at this stage or at any stage, the Prosecution has the obligation to disclosure, but it's within the scope of the Rules and Procedures. They could and they shouldn't be the investigator and the detective for the Defence team. As for the authenticity of some documents which might be a subject matter in the trial stage, I hope the parties will bear in mind the comments of the Pre-Trial Judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: With the permission of the Court, maybe I shall clarify something, Your Honour. As it was mentioned by the Defence counsel in the initial appearance, the Defence counsel referred to millions of documents. And we -- I believe that we indicated to the Court that we were not aware of those millions of documents. We have submitted documents which are relevant to that case, and I believe that there's probably in all total about a hundred documents that we've submitted for the supporting material. I would need to verify the precise amount, especially for the material in support of the amended indictment. It was one binder, and I think that it was about that. Maybe 75 or a hundred documents. So I'm not aware as we also informed the Court at the initial appearance about the tens of millions of documents. But of the material we submitted or transferred to the Defence, if the Defence within those hundred or more documents have any question, then we of course will answer his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope the parties could meet after this sitting to clarify this issue. But the principle is that the disclosure should be within the scope of the Rules and Procedures. Regarding the disclosure obligation under Rule 66(A)(ii), the Prosecution indicated that at the Status Conference of the 3rd November 2003 that it fulfilled its obligation under this Rule except for 25 to 30 per cent of the documents which still needed to be translated from B/C/S to English or from English to B/C/S. Has the translation been completed by now and has it been provided to the Defence team? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On the issue of the disclosure, we met with the Defence counsel prior to this hearing. And we informed him that there was several documents and material that was ready for him. He indicated to us how he would prefer us to transmit the documents. This will be done. From the documents, I believe that there are two or three still-outstanding translation to come. But as soon as we have, we will transmit it to the Defence counsel. As for the totality of the Rule 66(A)(ii) obligation, it is not fully completed because there's some verification in -- concerning certain matters that were raised that need to be fulfilled. But it is our intention to fulfil it as soon as possible to respect Rule 66(A)(ii). And part of the disclosure also is pursuant to 66(A)(ii) and 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Olujic, do you have any observations Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. concerning Rule 66(A)(ii) obligations?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not have any. As my learned friend has said today, I had a meeting with my colleagues from the OTP, and I was told that certain documents would be provided to us. Since this involves a large quantity of material, I asked that this material be delivered to me in Zagreb where I practice law. I don't think that this would pose a problem to the Prosecution. They promised to comply, and I expect to receive these documents within a short space of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The next issue is about Rule 68. Any observations from either parties regarding the disclosure of the exculpatory material pursuant to Rule 68? Yes, Ms. D'Aoust.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Like I informed the Court a little bit earlier, we have started to verify for exculpatory material. We are going in that disclosure to disclose those material. We understand that our obligation is an ongoing one, and we're doing the effort to fully respect that obligation also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any comments from Defence counsel on that issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have no comment. We expect this to be updated and to be carried out as soon as possible. Otherwise, we have no complaints or any other comments regarding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And another issue is the inspection of the materials. The Defence requested to inspect the books, documents, photographs or other objects in the Prosecutor's custody. Any issue to be raised in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no. I have nothing to raise. However, the strategy of our Defence is such that we are focussing on the time relevant for the indictment. So all of the materials, videotapes, and photographs, I will request them following the additional material that I will receive. And I do not expect to encounter any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Under Rule 65 ter (H), the Pre-Trial Judge shall record the points of agreement and disagreement on matters of law and fact. In this connection, the Pre-Trial Judge may order the parties to file written submissions with either the Pre-Trial Judge or the Trial Chamber. Did the parties already meet on this matter? Could they reach the agreement or disagreement on certain matters? It is the intention of the Trial Chamber to ask the parties in due course to file a document summarising those points of agreement and disagreement they should reach. And you are, therefore, encouraged to meet and consider this matter as soon as possible. Any progress in this aspect?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We haven't -- Defence counsel and Prosecution haven't met yet to discuss such matter. It is something that was briefly mentioned before, and I think that it is something that both parties envisioned seriously. But it has not been at the present time done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well -- yes, Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing to add, Your Honour. My learned friend has stated the facts as they are. I believe that very soon we will be able to find an agreement on agreed facts in order to facilitate the work of all of us, and especially our efforts aimed at establishing the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I appreciate the effort made by the two parties in this aspect. We hope we could speed up the preparation work in this case. At this stage, are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise? From the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is one last issue that I wanted to raise with the Court. As the Court may know, and I've raised it prior this hearing with my colleague, Mr. Olujic is acting for Mr. Rajic in this case. But in another case, Mr. Olujic also act for another accused. And we believe that during the initial appearance on the other accused, the possibility of a conflict of interest was raised. And since this case is, of course, related to it, we believe that it was our duty just to inform the Court that there may be a possibility of a conflict of interest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you for your information. What's your position on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: Of course we understand that the decision on the fact that if there is or not a conflict of interest is not up at all to the Prosecutor. But we would like to indicate that we have serious concern that there may be a possible conflict of interest. And by saying this, it has nothing to do, and I wouldn't want the Defence counsel to understand that I'm putting his professionalism in question, but I thought that it was our duty to raise it and to express our concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Your concern is registered here in the transcript. Could I hear from the Defence, Mr. Olujic, on this issue. Frankly speaking, I myself am not familiar with the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned friend is right when she says that just prior to entering the courtroom we discussed this issue; namely, there is proceedings going before this trial against Mr. Jadranko Prlic and Mr. Bruno Stojic and others. And Mr. Stojic has entrusted me with his Defence. Before I agreed to act as Defence counsel for Mr. Stojic, I have naturally studied and checked all the allegations to determine whether there is a conflict of interest. This is my professional responsibility. The code of ethics, both here before this Tribunal and in the country where I come from, mandates that I do this. I spoke about this with both of my clients, both with Mr. Rajic and with Mr. Stojic. Both of them expressed no reservations, and they insisted that I defend them here at this Tribunal. I work together with my co-counsel, Doris Kosta, who is an attorney-at-law in Split. We work together in this case. Why do I bring this up? I bring this up because should a conflict of interest arise, I would be the first one to step down, or rather I would choose which client I would defend. Since this is first and foremost the right of the accused, meaning not the right of the Prosecutor or Defence counsel or the Chamber, but rather the right of the accused that is enshrined and protected by main documents of this Tribunal, I believe that it is the decision of the accused that should be taken into account. However, the other case that I'm appearing in is also the case heard by Trial Chamber I, meaning the same Chamber. Therefore, should the Chamber question the moral dignity and professionalism of the Defence, then the Chamber would make certain decisions in order to protect the interests of the accused. Therefore, I am in contact with the officials from the Registry and I turned over to them written statements of both of my clients. And together with that, I provided a broad interpretation of the conflict of interest as a concept and also attached some information showing that there is no conflict of interest in this case or in these two cases. However, we never know what can emerge, and should the conflict of interest arise, then I'm sure we would undertake all steps in order to safeguard the principles of justice, especially since there are several Defence counsel in each case. We have the lead counsel and the co-counsel, and each of them can take over should there be a need. Your Honour, this is in brief my position. I believed that the Chamber was aware of this situation; however, I see that I might have been wrong because so far I have not received a decision on my appointment, neither I nor the rest of my team. Therefore, I hope that we will receive a decision from the Registry on that issue, although we know that the final word rests with the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As I said before, this is the first time for me as a Pre-Trial Judge in this case to hear there might be a conflict of interest concerning the counsel. I have to say, first of all, this matter is within the jurisdiction of the Registrar at this stage. If we came to the trial stage and this matter greatly affects the interests of the accused, the Trial Chamber may interfere in this issue. But generally speaking, generally speaking, it's within the mandate of the Registrar. So any filings should go to the Registrar. Secondly, we have no doubt about the professional responsibility and the code of ethics on the part of the Defence counsel at this stage. And it's very difficult at this stage to predict how the trial proceedings will go. For instance, if one of the accused plead guilty or for his own interests he will blame the other witness -- the other accused. So there might be a potential, potential conflict of interest in the future. Lastly, I believe the free will of the accused should be taken into due account because it is, after all, the accuseds who retain the counsel. And what is important in this aspect whether the accused is informed, well informed, about legal consequences of the conflict of interest of the counsels in this matter. It is a very technical issue concerning the conflict of interest of the counsels, and nobody could predict what will happen in the future, in the middle of the trial, or even after the trial. So I will consult with the Registrar on this issue to see whether they could get in touch with the accused himself to make sure the accused, Mr. Rajic, has made a decision free, out of his free will and well informed about all the consequences of that potential issue. I think that's all I could say at this stage. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'AOUST
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So the hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
